question: A lift station control panel shows a high wet well level alarm at 2 a.m. Which response comes first for the on-call operator?
correctAnswer: Acknowledge the alarm and check the pump and level readings
explanation: A high level alarm signals that inflow may be outpacing pumping, so the operator acknowledges it and checks pump status and level readings before deciding the next step.
options: Wait until the morning crew arrives to look at the panel and decide what to do next
Acknowledge the alarm and check the pump and level readings
Reset the alarm and leave the station without checking
Turn off the main breaker and lock the station gate
optionA: Wait until the morning crew arrives to look at the panel and decide what to do next
optionB: Acknowledge the alarm and check the pump and level readings
optionC: Reset the alarm and leave the station without checking
optionD: Turn off the main breaker and lock the station gate

question: Which pump type is commonly fitted in a lift station to pass rags and small solids in raw wastewater?
correctAnswer: A submersible non-clog centrifugal pump
explanation: Submersible non-clog centrifugal pumps use a wide passage impeller that passes rags and small solids, so they suit raw wastewater lift stations.
options: A centrifugal pump with a multistage diffuser
A positive displacement gear pump for clean water
A submersible non-clog centrifugal pump
A shallow well jet pump with a small impeller
optionA: A centrifugal pump with a multistage diffuser
optionB: A positive displacement gear pump for clean water
optionC: A submersible non-clog centrifugal pump
optionD: A shallow well jet pump with a small impeller

correctAnswer: A calibrated four-gas detector
explanation: A calibrated four-gas detector measures oxygen, flammable gas, hydrogen sulfide and carbon monoxide, which are the readings used to judge entry air.

A portable turbidity meter with a sample cell
A magnetic flow meter
A calibrated four-gas detector

Flow rises steadily through the night after a rain event
Flow spikes for ten minutes when a pump starts
Flow drops each time the wet well pump stops
optionA: Flow falls to near zero and stays flat all night after the evening peak has passed
optionB: Flow rises steadily through the night after a rain event
optionC: Flow spikes for ten minutes when a pump starts
optionD: Flow drops each time the wet well pump stops

Turn off the level floats so the alarm stops sounding

question: A detector lowered into a manhole reads 16 percent oxygen. Which action follows from that reading?
correctAnswer: Ventilate the space and retest before any entry is considered
explanation: Oxygen at 16 percent is below the level needed for safe entry, so the space is ventilated and retested before entry is considered.
options: Enter quickly and finish the work before the reading changes
Switch the detector off and rely on smell instead of the instrument reading
Ventilate the space and retest before any entry is considered
Send in a second worker to confirm the reading by feel

optionB: Switch the detector off and rely on smell instead of the instrument reading
optionC: Ventilate the space and retest before any entry is considered

question: Two night flow charts cover the same sewer. One night shows a minimum flow of 8 L/s and the next shows 22 L/s after a day of rain. Which conclusion fits the change?
correctAnswer: Rainwater is entering the sewer through infiltration or inflow
explanation: Overnight customer use is low and steady, so a jump in minimum night flow after rain points toward rainwater entering through infiltration or inflow.
options: Customer water use tripled overnight for no clear reason and then fell back by morning
The flow meter failed and recorded the same value twice
The sewer cleaned itself and now carries less flow
Rainwater is entering the sewer through infiltration or inflow
optionA: Customer water use tripled overnight for no clear reason and then fell back by morning
optionB: The flow meter failed and recorded the same value twice
optionC: The sewer cleaned itself and now carries less flow
optionD: Rainwater is entering the sewer through infiltration or inflow

question: A jetting crew cleaned 900 m on Monday and 600 m on Tuesday, when a buried service slowed the work. How should the supervisor compare the two days when planning the next week?
correctAnswer: Plan the next week from the average rate and note the buried service as the cause of the slow day
explanation: An average rate gives a fair planning figure, and noting the buried service explains the slow day so similar streets are scheduled with enough time.
options: Discard the Tuesday record because it makes the crew look slow and plan from Monday alone
Plan the next week from the average rate and note the buried service as the cause of the slow day
Plan every street at the Monday rate and ignore the Tuesday result when setting the weekly schedule
Count both days as 900 m so the weekly total looks even and the report stays simple

optionD: Count both days as 900 m so the weekly total looks even and the report stays simple

question: A lift station alarm panel shows no alarms, yet the wet well level has risen above the high level float. Which fault does that combination point toward?
correctAnswer: A failed alarm float or a fault in the alarm circuit
explanation: When the level passes the high float without an alarm, the float or the alarm circuit has likely failed, so the alarm path is checked before the station is trusted.
options: A pump that is running faster than its rating and drawing the level down
A wet well that has been cleaned recently
A failed alarm float or a fault in the alarm circuit
A force main that is flowing freely
optionA: A pump that is running faster than its rating and drawing the level down
optionB: A wet well that has been cleaned recently
optionC: A failed alarm float or a fault in the alarm circuit
